sections.h2: Where Casselberry sits and what buyers notice
sections.html:
Casselberry is at the southern end of Seminole County, about ten miles north of downtown Orlando. Interstate 4 is five minutes away, State Road 436 and U.S. 17-92 cross the city, and commute time is often the first thing a buyer weighs. Put drive times and road access in your listing.

The city covers approximately 8 square miles, so neighborhoods are small and close together. Lakes are a draw, and the larger ones include Lake Howell, Lake Kathryn and the Triplet Chain of Lakes, so name the nearest one in your listing. If a buyer asks about schools, point them to Seminole County Public Schools to confirm attendance zones for your address instead of promising one. Seminole County, not the city, assesses, bills and records property, which keeps the paperwork in one place.

A short list of recurring dates governs every Casselberry owner's year.

Property tax calendar for Seminole County
DateEvent
January 1Date of assessment for all property
March 1Deadline to apply for homestead exemption or agricultural classification
April 1Deadline for personal property returns
Mid-AugustProposed tax (TRIM) notices mailed
25 days after mailingDeadline for real property petitions to the Value Adjustment Board
NovemberValue Adjustment Board hearings begin; Tax Collector mails bills

January 1 through March 1 is the regular filing window for the current tax year. A filing made between March 2 and December 31 counts as pre-filing for the next year.

sections.h2: When the tax bill is due and when it turns late
sections.html:
Bills go out from the Tax Collector in November. Pay that month and take off 4 percent; the discount falls by a point each month, reaching 1 percent in February. Nothing comes off in March, and April 1 is when unpaid taxes turn delinquent.

The state also offers an installment prepayment plan, which requires an application to the tax collector by May 1. Partial payments before delinquency are accepted at the collector's discretion. The Seminole County Tax Collector can explain how either would work on your parcel.

Look at each year's bill before you list. A buyer's title agent will, and a surprise costs time.

sections.h2: Trusts and lady bird deeds before a sale
sections.html:
Both are possible, but talk to an attorney about the tax effects first. In one revenue advisement, a lady bird deed on the facts presented moved no present beneficial interest, so no documentary stamp tax was due. That was one advisement on one set of facts, and it is not a rule for every deed.

The same agency adds that no specific exemption covers deeds moving Florida real property for estate planning. Its taxable list includes quit claim deeds and contracts for deed. Moving title usually counts as a change of ownership for Save Our Homes unless an exception fits, such as a transfer between spouses.

If a family member's name must come off title before a sale, the usual signing rule applies: a writing with two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01.

sections.h2: How much has the Save Our Homes cap allowed lately?
sections.html:
Recent caps have tracked inflation closely. The chart revised in January 2026 lists 3.4 percent inflation and a 3.0 percent cap for 2024, 2.9 percent for both in 2025, and 2.7 percent for both in 2026. Because the cap is whichever is lower, 3 percent or the inflation change, a long-held Casselberry homestead can be assessed well below market.

That gap is the savings a seller carries. At sale the buyer's assessment resets to just value. You, if you buy again in Florida, may port part of that gap to the new house. The portability form travels with the new property's homestead application, due March 1, and the new house must be your permanent residence by January 1.

  • Gather your last three tax bills to see how the assessed and just values compare.
  • Confirm that the homestead exemption is still active on the latest roll.
  • Keep a copy of the portability form with your closing file.

sections.h2: Checklist for the weeks before closing
sections.html:
The title agent runs most of this, but you speed things up by having documents ready.

  • Order a payoff from your lender and ask whether a prepayment charge applies.
  • Check with the city for open permits on additions, sheds or roof work.
  • Confirm that every owner on title can sign, or that a legal representative has authority.
  • Ask the title agent how the November tax bill will be split at closing.
  • Cancel or transfer water, sewer and garbage service, which the city provides as municipal utilities.

Once signed, the deed goes to the county clerk to be recorded. The new owner then has until the next March 1 to file for an exemption of their own. Keep your settlement statement with your tax papers for the year.

sections.h2: What about tenants, inheritance and missed payments?
sections.html:
For a rented house, the notice depends on the problem. Nonpayment needs 3 days' written notice, which skips weekends and court holidays. A curable lease violation gives the tenant 7 days to cure, and an incurable one gives 7 days to vacate. When a landlord wins in court, the sheriff posts a 24 hour notice before returning possession.

An inherited house usually needs probate authority first. A shorter court process, summary administration, is open if the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the owner has been dead more than 2 years. Deaths after 2004 carry no Florida estate tax.

An owner behind on the mortgage faces a foreclosure sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. A sale before that date leaves you more control over terms.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready on a short clock
sections.html:
A quick sale rewards small, inexpensive moves. Clear the yard and garage, fix anything that leaks or will not open, and take clear photos in daylight. Keep a folder with your deed, recent utility bills, appliance manuals and any repair receipts, so a buyer can see the house has been looked after. If a roof, air conditioner or plumbing job is unfinished, say so up front. A buyer who learns about it from you can price it; one who discovers it late tends to walk away or ask for a steep discount.

When more than one person owns the house, settle early who will sign and where each of you will be on closing day.

List or sell for cash, the test is the same: how much you keep, when you close and how likely the deal is to fall apart. Check funds or loan paperwork, read any repair terms twice, and ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement on your favorite offer. Raise questions about it days ahead, not at the signing table. Also decide in advance how long you can wait. A seller with a firm move date is better placed to turn down a weak offer, and one without a date should say so up front so the buyer's schedule fits yours.

faqs.a: Yes. The city lies in the county's southern end. County offices handle your assessment, tax bill and recording.

faqs.q: When do I apply for homestead in Seminole County?
faqs.a: By March 1. January 1 to March 1 is the regular window, and applications filed between March 2 and December 31 count as pre-filing for the next year.

faqs.q: What discount applies if I pay early?
faqs.a: Pay in November for 4 percent off, then the discount drops one point a month to 1 percent in February. March has none, and April 1 starts delinquency.

faqs.q: Does a lady bird deed avoid the deed tax?
faqs.a: Not always. The state agency reached that result on one set of facts where the owners kept full powers, so get an attorney's read on yours.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest my Casselberry value?
faqs.a: It is 25 days after the mid-August TRIM mailing. The notice itself states the filing deadline.
